newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Valley execs decry US tech spending waste.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Valley execs decry US tech spending waste.

text.p: A group of prominent Silicon Valley executives, led by outspoken Cypress Semiconductor Corp Chief Executive T.J. Rodgers, Tuesday repeated their call for an end to U.S. funding for technology programs they consider wasteful.

The business leaders, including chief executives of Advanced Micro Devices, LSI Logic, Seagate Technology and Sun Microsystems Inc, have endorsed a statement opposing what they label "corporate welfare" for the high tech industry.

Senator Sam Brownback, a Kansas Republican who succeeded former Majority Leader Robert Dole, appeared with several of the executives at Cypress's headquarters here to propose a blue ribbon panel be formed to draw up a list of federal programs for elimination.
The group would be modeled after the military base closings panel in a bid to cut through legislators' vested interests in their own home industries, Brownback said.

In recent testimony in Congress, Rodgers questioned the wisdom of the Commerce Department's Advanced Technology Program, including a $500 million NASA program he said aimed to produce gallium arsenide wafers in space at a cost of up to $1 million per wafer.
Wafers are the basic material used to make computer chips, with the vast majority currently made from silicon.
"General Motors should not get subsidies to learn how to paint cars better," Rodgers said in a statement.
Rodgers has previously argued that Congress should vote on a broad package of subsidies identified for elimination by an independent commission, such as the one Brownback is proposing.
Brownback is chairman of a Senate subcommittee on oversight of government management, which is part of the Senate Committee on Government Affairs.
"We in the business did not coin the term corporate welfare," said Rodgers.
Rodgers said government-backed funding was used by legislators as a means of gaining favor with businessmen.
